claims.claim: Each great flood drawn here, 1771 to 1985, put water into Shockoe Bottom, the river streets below downtown and over Mayo Island; the mapped 1969 flood also covered the Manchester flats.
claims.note: the plates show it; HA-410 maps 1969

claims.claim: Since 1994 a floodwall built by the Corps with the city has kept the river out of Shockoe Bottom and most of the Manchester flats.
claims.note: "most": the earthen levee east of I-95 is not in our data

claims.claim: The highest water since stood about 18 ft below the overtopping stage (41 - 22.7).
Aug. 30, 2004: about 10 in of rain on the land draining to the Bottom; the James far below flood stage.
Water drawn level at the City Locks height, at the foot of Pear Street, on today's lidar, with the buildings of the year.
claims.note: Locks at foot of Pear Street: OFR 70-51 via datums.md

claims.claim: Fig. 2 gauge 15 ft at 17th and Main (level less lidar ground).
claims.note: counts rc3 boxes shockoe 1972 market depthFt

claims.claim: Depth tones to 20 ft and more; everyday water light blue; x-ray band; 11 ft is about 6 px on a whole plate.
Cream = shown standing by sources; grey dashed = earlier map or photo, not ascertained for the year.
Hatch = range of an estimate; cross-hatch = ground whose protection the data cannot show; dry twin aligned pixel for pixel.
Older datum converted about 1.03 ft lower at Richmond.
Shockoe Creek runs south from north of I-64 to the James near 17th and Dock.
The creek's lower course was put into conduits in the 1920s (1923-1928 project).
claims.note: lawsuit dates the Arch to 1926-27 (BizSense); both within the 1920s

claims.claim: Lowest point a pit beside the 17th Street Market at 13.4 ft; 17th and Main 21.6 ft.
Manchester flats run from the riverbank to about Commerce Road.
James above Westham drains 6,753 sq mi; no dam on the river stores floods before Richmond.
claims.note: before-the-wall.md: dams above Richmond are run-of-river (WDR 1986)

claims.claim: Gathright Dam lowers Richmond flood peaks by about 1.5 percent (FEMA).
In 1969 the water rose about 1.3 ft from the Locks to the Mayo Bridge, then more than 50 ft through the falls to the Boulevard Bridge.
Table: levels and ranges; acres; buildings in water of those shown.
Fig. 3 strip depths at 17th and Main per flood.
USGS OFR 70-51 gives 38 ft for May 27, 1771, from a Corps report, on the old Weather Bureau scale near the Mayo Bridge; early stages set from authenticated diary accounts.
About 38 ft at the Locks, about 2.5 ft above Agnes.
Other accounts give 30 ft and 45 ft on unstated bases.
Henrico County: buildings and boats destroyed in Richmond; about 150 died along the river.
Fig. 4: hatch to 41 ft; six buildings and the 1737 street plan in the frame.
claims.note: log step 62: the 1788 scene is the 1737 plan plus buildings dated before 1788, six in the frame

claims.claim: Crest about 26.5 ft at the Locks.
USGS plotted about a dozen 1936 high-water marks.
NWS history: serious flooding of industrial and business sections.
Fig. 5 counts.
Camille remnants; 28.64 ft at 6 a.m. Aug. 22, 1969; 27.6 ft today.
Advance warning limited losses; serious flooding in the lower elevations.
HA-410 extent: valley floor to about Main Street Station, all of Mayo Island, Manchester flats to about Commerce Road with the sewage plant, Gillies Creek valley through Fulton.
claims.note: the research's reading of the plate

claims.claim: The levee then at Shockoe Creek's mouth had to stop pumping during Camille for structural reasons.
claims.note: FIS 1998 p. 9 and 2025 Table 5 p. 27, via fis.md

claims.claim: Fig. 6 counts; HA-410 water reached about as far up the valley.
36.5 ft on the gauge datum of the time at 4 p.m. June 23, 1972; 35.5 ft today; sign at Dock and Pear marks 35.5, 17 ft above ground.
Westham 313,000 cfs, still the record.
Evacuations from June 22 morning; by June 23 downtown lost power and drinking water; purification plant flooded; 4 of 5 bridges closed; National Guard cordoned parts of the city.
The older creek-mouth levee was overtopped in 1972.
Sign: 13 local deaths, over $140 million local damage; NOAA: 5 deaths along the James.
Drawing: 220.4 acres; 226 of 1,173; median 10.2 ft; deepest 33.2 ft; gauges 15, 11, 19 ft.
What "shown" includes: dating, Sanborn traces with the 1974 photo; 273 grey; 40 outbuildings and 23 footprints left out; 1974 photo two years after.
Fig. 7: 17th and Dock 19 ft; the Dock and Pear sign a few hundred feet east.
claims.note: datums.md: sign "a few hundred feet" from the gauge

claims.claim: 30.76 ft on Nov. 7, 1985 (old datum), about 29.7 today; second-highest crest since gauges began, after Agnes.
NWS history: several blocks of commercial and industrial buildings flooded.
Congress authorized the wall the next year (Nov. 17, 1986).
No public air photo of the 1980s found; 180 grey.
District report Sept. 1980; Chief of Engineers Nov. 16, 1981; WRDA 1986 signed Nov. 17, 1986; $91.8 million; must include protection for the wastewater plant (quoted, 12 words).
City utilities: approval followed the 1985 flood.
Construction began Nov. 5, 1988.
claims.note: not reread by the second reader

claims.claim: 1993 ceiling $134 million; dedicated Oct. 21, 1994; final cost $143 million (one source).
North wall about 4,277 ft, 12th and Byrd to 21st and East Cary, across the valley mouth; 4 to 30 ft above ground.
South line about 13,046 ft of concrete wall and earthen levee with bin wall; west of the Manchester Bridge to I-95, then south and west across the railroad to high ground near Goodes Street.
Just west of the Mayo Bridge a gravity U-wall, 43 ft from top to river's edge.
About 750 acres: 150 Shockoe, 600 Manchester.
19 openings closed with gates.
No surveyed top found; NWS: overtopped at 41 ft; about 5.5 ft above Agnes.
claims.note: fis.md: neither FIS prints a top

claims.claim: City: northern wall built for an average recurrence of about 280 years; FEMA 1998: 3 ft above the 100-year, does not protect against the 500-year.
Fig. 9: with today's wall, 111.0 acres outside the wall; 22 of 1,101 buildings.
Fran remnants; 23.75 ft Sept. 8, 1996; about 22.7 today, perhaps 1 ft more (datum era unknown); about 18 ft below the overtopping stage.
January 1996 some gates shut, Dock Street among them; in Fran some gates.
Nov. 2020 crest 16.96 ft early Nov. 14 (04:48 to 04:54 EST).
17th Street closure on Dock Street shut at noon Nov. 12; Brander Street gate that evening.
Dock Street closure shut again Feb. 2025, first since 2020.
As of 2011 the James had never forced closing all gates.
Fig. 10 acres outside the wall.
At the 1972 height: no wall 527.1 acres, 246 of 412, deepest 29.1 ft; Hull Street at the Mayo Bridge about 14 ft; with the wall flats dry, 41.5 acres outside; 212.8 acres and 54 buildings not known.
Concrete parts in OSM; the 7,170 ft earthen levee is not.
Lidar ridge along I-95 at about 43 to 45 ft; cannot tell levee from highway fill.
1986 law required protecting the wastewater plant; the plant stands east of I-95.
The drawing cross-hatches that ground with no depth, out of the counts; edges follow the levee's possible courses.
Gaston ashore in S.C. morning of Aug. 29; a tropical depression when its center crossed into Virginia Aug. 30; passed well southeast of Richmond.
Storms formed along a boundary from Hampton Roads to Richmond, drifted northwest and stalled over the city from early afternoon into the evening.
Forecasts called for an inch or two that day.
claims.note: p. 1: NAM and GFS 1 to 2 in

claims.claim: Fig. 13: solid to about 28 ft, hatch to 35; openings dashed (open); pool held on the city side.
Watershed about 12 sq mi (7,780 acres); average about 10 in, range 8.6 to 11.6; about 2.2 billion gallons; most between 2 and 9 p.m.; 1.3 to 2.2 in each hour 2 to 8 p.m.
Wettest hour about 2.2 in, 5 to 6 p.m., about a 10-year one-hour rain at a point.
About 10 in in six hours reaches or passes Atlas 14's 1,000-year six-hour point amount, 8.04 in, by every estimate but one (AORC 7.9).
First flash-flood warning 3:58 p.m.
claims.note: Style Weekly quoting the weather service

claims.claim: Storm Events starts the flash flooding at 4:30 in a time it labels EST, perhaps 5:30 EDT.
claims.note: inspection rc3 R1: not stated as exact

claims.claim: The Bottom is a bowl whose lowest streets lie below the riverfront strip of Dock Street, rail embankments and the wall.
Runoff off Church Hill and the Capitol slope into the Bottom; most water came together at 17th and Main.
Gates stood open; the city closes them for river forecasts; the James peaked 14,800 cfs at 9:15 p.m., about a third of the 42,000 cfs minor-flood flow.
Spill test: pool first reaches the James at about 19.1 ft at 17th and Dock; with openings open at street level about 21.7 ft via the Dock Street opening near 18th.
FEMA Shockoe Creek model: 1% level near Dock Street 19.4 ft.
claims.note: Floodway Data section A, PDF p. 70; panel 37P

claims.claim: Reported depths imply water above both; a rough weir calculation puts the reports between an open riverfront and the openings alone; a question for a hydraulic model; the wall's effect is not known.
claims.note: outlet.json: 23 to 24 ft open line, 32 to 35 ft openings only

claims.claim: No surveyed high-water marks found; up to 10 ft; Havana '59 13 ft up the dining-room wall (owner); Bottoms Up 6 ft 2 in above a 3-ft step; law office 7 ft; rapids at 15th and Main (a developer); Main Street Station escaped damage.
Depths imply 24 to 35 ft; drawing at about 28 ("up to 10 feet" at the lowest blocks); about 9 ft at the market; 31.4 acres; 99 of 1,059.
Fig. 16: pin A where most water came together; pin B at Havana '59's usual address.
claims.note: usual address: notes.json, not stated in the source

claims.claim: Eight died in flash floods in and around Richmond, three in the city; two in Gillies Creek about a mile east of the Bottom; no source places a death in the Bottom.
Fire crews took people out by raft and boat; about two dozen waited on the Bottoms Up second-floor deck.
About 20 blocks roped off and condemned until inspected; $20 million property damage in the city.
Almost no one carried flood insurance: the wall took the Bottom out of the mapped flood zone; lenders had stopped requiring it.
Aug. 2009 lawsuit alleging the city's handling of sewer gates and a pumping station made flooding worse; no outcome found.
claims.note: research searched for a ruling or settlement and found none

claims.claim: About 100 inlets moved and added; flap gates into the canal; about $20 million over a decade; 2018: more than three times the capacity of 2004.
No rain since has matched Gaston's over the watershed (AORC); officials said one could flood the Bottom again.

The limits as listed: bathtub fill; one height; Mayo rise assumed from 1969; held level west of the bridge; today's ground on a 5 m grid; wall top; levee; old creek-mouth levee not drawn; grey buildings; estimated heights; topped buildings left off; Gaston depths; rain 40 percent at a point.

Drawn with isoscape; levels, city, counts and rain in code with Claude; sheets independently inspected and fact checked in three rounds in Nov. 2026 by a Claude agent that had not made them; corrected wording followed.
